subject: Order Form / MSA - indemnity delegation and scope questions
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@acmeinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@stellarnet.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form - indemnity language (first pass)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team reviewed the indemnity sections and attached a marked-up copy with changes. High-level asks:
- Broad IP indemnity flowing from vendor to customer for third-party IP claims tied to the service (customer is asking vendor to defend & indemnify).
- Remove the carve that limits vendor indemnity when customer uses outputs or modifies models without vendor supervision.
- Add explicit insurance requirement (E&O) and a notice timeline for claims.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a mutual IP indemnity (i.e., both parties indemnify for their own infringing acts) rather than the vendor-first language, or provide alternative language that addresses our concerns.

Attaching: acme_redlines_20260528.docx (redlines)

Thanks,
Claire

Sr. Contracts Manager
Acme Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-05-28T12:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form - indemnity language (first pass)

Hi Claire — thanks for the redlines and the clear notes. Quick response while we loop in legal:

1) Mutual approach: Redwood is open to a mutual IP indemnity for traditional patent/copyright/software claims originating from the parties' own deliverables.
2) Carve for customer modifications / derivative outputs: we need a narrow carve where Redwood won’t indemnify if the customer materially modifies the product or uses it in an unsupported way (e.g., retraining with customer data and then claiming infringement). We can propose language that preserves customer use of outputs for their business while protecting Redwood from claims arising solely from customer modifications.
3) Cap and remedy: business would prefer an indemnity cap tied to fees (12-months of fees) or a fixed cap; legal to confirm.
4) Defense control & settlement: Redwood generally seeks to control defense for third-party claims (with obligation to consult / not settle adverse to the customer without consent).

I attached a high-level counter redline with suggested compromise language to speed review. Neha — can you take the redlines and propose specific MSA text for the IP + third-party flow? Aditya — FYI on the carve ideas from product side.

Attachments: redwood_counter_redlines_20260528.docx

Date: 2026-06-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form - indemnity language (first pass)

Marissa / Claire — I reviewed Acme's markups and Marissa's suggested compromises. Below is Redwood legal's recommended package to propose back to Acme. I kept the wording tight to avoid open-ended exposure while addressing Acme's commercial/compliance needs. If the business accepts, I can convert this into a tracked-change MSA redline.

Summary of recommended position (high level):
- Mutual IP indemnity for claims arising from a party's materials or services (i.e., vendor indemnifies for vendor-originating infringing code/models; customer indemnifies for customer-originating modifications, content, or prompts).
- Carveouts: Redwood will not be responsible for claims arising from (a) customer's modifications, (b) customer's failure to follow documented instructions, (c) customer's combination of the service with non-Redwood products that creates the alleged infringing functionality. We will explicitly preserve indemnity for Redwood-origin components and pre-packaged models we ship.
- Defense & cooperation: Redwood will have the right to assume defense with counsel of our choice; Redwood will not settle a claim that imposes an obligation on the customer without customer's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld). Customer must provide prompt written notice (within 30 days) of claims and cooperate in the defense.
- Cap: Recommend cap = the greater of (i) $1,000,000 and (ii) fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim. Rationale: balances commercial risk and provides meaningful protection for Acme.
- Third-party claim flow: indemnity only applies if customer notifies Redwood promptly and (if Redwood requests) provides control of defense; Redwood will cover reasonable mitigation costs (e.g., reengineering to avoid the claimed IP) if the claim is valid.
- Insurance: we are willing to commit to maintain E&O insurance at commercially reasonable limits; we propose to insert a 3rd-party certificate requirement on request for enterprise orders.

Open items for Acme (we propose to ask):
- Whether Acme will accept the mutual IP approach with the carve language above.
- Whether the proposed cap is acceptable (1M or 12 months' fees).
- Any specific escrow/novation requests for continuity in the event of vendor insolvency — Redwood is open to discussing limited transition assistance but cannot put full escrow of IP in the MSA.

I will draft tracked-change text if you want to proceed. Business note: if Acme insists on vendor-first unlimited IP indemnity with no carve, we will need to escalate.

Attachment: legal_marked_up_MSA_20260601.pdf

-Neha

From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@acmeinc.com>

Date: 2026-06-02T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form - indemnity language (first pass)

Thanks Neha — appreciate the pragmatic approach. A few clarifying points from Acme legal after reviewing your summary:

1) Defense control: Acme will consider allowing Redwood to control the defense if Redwood commits not to (a) undermine Acme's public-facing position (no admission/consent to injunctive relief binding Acme), and (b) not settle for an amount that confers liability on Acme without Acme's prior written consent. We need to see that spelled out.
2) Cap: 1M floor + 12 months' fees is workable; confirm whether that floor scales for larger enterprise orders (we may ask for a higher floor if ARR > $10M).
3) Escrow/novation: Acme's concern is continuity if a claim materially impacts service. We are not asking for broad IP escrow, but we want a narrow transition assistance + data export/hand-off guarantee in an insolvency/termination-for-convenience scenario.

Also attaching a short list of Qs (acme_questions_20260602.pdf) around timing for notice, subrogation rights, and whether Redwood's insurance will explicitly cover defense costs.

Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through one redlined MSA snapshot instead of iterating docs back-and-forth?

Thanks,
Claire

Date: 2026-06-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form - indemnity language (first pass)

Claire — good plan. Let's do a short call to finalize the compromise language. Proposed times: 2026-06-03 09:00 or 14:00 PT — which works for you?

To summarize the position we'll present on the call (so you have it in advance):
- Mutual IP indemnity with the carve language Neha outlined (customer modifications, combinations, and unsupported retraining excluded).
- Defense: Redwood can assume defense; Redwood will not settle in a way that creates liability for Acme without written consent.
- Cap: greater of $1M or 12 months' fees (we are open to discussing a higher floor for very large deals).
- Insurance: Redwood will maintain E&O and provide certificate on request for the enterprise order.
- Transition assistance: Redwood agrees to limited transition assistance on termination or insolvency (data export, reasonable cooperation) — we'll confirm timeframes and operational SLAs on the call.

I'll send an invite once you confirm a time. If the call goes well we'll produce a single tracked redline (DocuSign-ready) that reflects the agreed changes.
